project.name: agent-api
project.description:
Service-to-service contract for remote tool supply (V9 §18 / §91).
Members: RemoteToolCatalog (the port), RemoteTool (one contributed tool) and RemoteToolCall (the channel a tool talks back through).
Why the module exists. integration.mcp.client.application implemented com.xander.lab.agent.application.AgentTool and AgentPromptSection, and AgentMcpServerService called AgentToolRegistry#invalidate() -- five implementation statements pointing integration -> agent, crossing the dinqor-platform-integration / dinqor-agent deployment-unit boundary. After the split that means the integration service cannot be built without the agent service's implementation classes, and the call goes the wrong way: the *provider* of remote tools was reaching into its *consumer*. The port and its data move to a module both sides may depend on, and the direction becomes integration -> agent-api <- agent.
Package note: this module's package is com.xander.lab.agent.spi, NOT com.xander.lab.agent.api. The three sibling contracts that sit inside a domain's own namespace (agent-api / automation-api / studio-api) hit a collision the content-api / core-api / payment-api ones do not: those domains already own com.xander.lab.<domain>.api as their *frontend HTTP* layer (controllers, VOs, request bodies). Declaring the contract there would put one package in two jars, and worse, would make the scanner classify the domain's own controllers as shared kernel -- every controller importing its own application layer would become an agent.api -> agent edge (inflating the backlog with dozens of statements) and a shared-kernel-reverse-dependency violation. So the contract takes the next free segment, spi, and SHARED_KERNEL lists agent.spi (dotted, matched longest-first). automation-api and studio-api hit the same collision; they take the same answer.
Why AgentTool itself is NOT here, which is the whole difficulty of this cut. AgentTool is the obvious candidate -- it is the interface integration used to implement -- but it is unusable as a contract type: * parametersSchema() returns com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode. ADR-1 says a contract module must stay serialization-framework agnostic, and CONTRACT_ALLOWED_IMPORT_PREFIXES is java. only. Moving AgentTool here would require widening that gate, which is exactly the super-common.jar §19 forbids. * It has 6 default members (promptSection / execute / reconcile / approvalReason / readOnly) plus a nested ProgressListener with 5 more, so every implementation would be coupled to agent's whole tool vocabulary. * 50 implementations, 41 of which override parametersSchema(). Moving the interface means touching all of them. So the cut does not move AgentTool. It adds a narrow port that answers only the questions the consumer actually asks, and keeps AgentTool where it is. The 50 implementations are untouched; the Jackson cut is confined to this port surface plus one adapter on each side. A port is a design freedom -- choose the shape that makes the implementation-side change degenerate.
Why the schema travels as String. RemoteTool#parametersSchemaJson returns the JSON Schema as text, and RemoteTool#invoke takes arguments and returns the result the same way. That is not a stylistic choice: JsonNode is what made AgentTool un-movable. It costs one parse on the agent side (cached in the adapter) and one toString on the provider side, against a call that is a network round trip. Verified byte-identical: RemoteMcpTool already held a parsed JsonNode, so schema.toString() -> readTree() reproduces the same tree and the rendered tool surface JSON does not change. That is what keeps this cut out of docs/contract-changes.yaml.
RemoteTool deliberately has no order() for its prompt section. Ordering is the renderer's policy, not the provider's data: every remote tool leaves the platform, so its guidance is a side-effect rule by definition, and the adapter maps it to AgentPromptSection.ORDER_SIDE_EFFECT. Carrying an int across the boundary would mean a second copy of that constant table in another module, free to drift.
What is deliberately NOT here yet: - Any of agent's own api layer (com.xander.lab.agent.api.*). It is the frontend HTTP contract (web / miniprogram), a different audience from the service-to-service one, and it joins a contract module only when that layer itself is split in Wave 2. - AgentDynamicToolSource / AgentToolRegistry. They are agent's in-process abstractions; the whole point of the port is that integration never sees them.
Known residual after this cut (recorded, not fixed): agent -> integration stays at 0 statements in both layers, but the agent-side adapter still has to be reachable as a Spring bean from the integration-owned McpToolSource -- in one process that is automatic, across two it becomes a network call. Same open question as BlogPublisher; see docs/migration/lib-extraction.md.
Zero dependencies, and that is the point. A contract that drags in a framework cannot be depended on by every service, and V9 §19 is explicit that the WebFlux Gateway must stay free of spring-webmvc. Nothing here may gain a compile dependency without a deliberate decision; test scope is fine.
